必.meaning: Every morning at seven, a <part>slash</part> of lightning strikes the same <part>heart</part> painted on the old barn door. Rain or shine, summer or winter, it never misses once. The farmers set their clocks by it: it happens <kanji>invariably</kanji>.
必.on: A <sound>hitch</sound>hiker waits by the barn each morning, knowing the flash will light up the road for the first car.
必.kun: Right after the flash, without fail, the farmer fries a <sound>ca</sound>rp, warms some <sound>na</sound>an and cheers '<sound>Rah</sound>, breakfast!'

冊.meaning: Someone has fitted a football <part>goal</part> into a tall wooden <part>frame</part> and filled it with giant leather books instead of a net. Every shot you score knocks one out onto the grass with a thud. Each is a dusty, heavy <kanji>tome</kanji>.
冊.on: Inside the cover of one, someone has pressed a flat, dried <sound>sats</sound>uma as a bookmark.
冊.kun: The goalkeeper reads it curled up on a <sound>fu</sound>ton, with a <sound>mee</sound>rkat peeking over her shoulder.

論.meaning: In the hushed <part>library</part>, two scholars burst into loud <part>speech</part>, waving scrolls and jabbing fingers at each other's noses. Books tumble off the shelves and the librarian shushes in vain. Neither will back down in their <kanji>argument</kanji>.
論.on: One scholar gets so cross he hurls a b<sound>ron</sound>ze bust of an old thinker across the room.
論.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, <sound>ge</sound>t out!' snaps the librarian, then sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' in the dust, while they keep yelling '<sound>Rah</sound>!': picking holes in each other.

容.meaning: A giant chef pours hot green jelly into a whole <part>valley</part>, then lays a glass <part>roof</part> over it to keep the flies off. Next morning she flips it out onto a vast plate: a wobbly copy of every hill and stream. The jelly took the valley's <kanji>form</kanji>.
容.on: On top she sets a tiny jelly <sound>yo</sound>-yo that bobs slowly down and up on a liquorice string.
容.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' squeals a mouse as she puts the leftover jelly in the fridge: put in to set.

振.meaning: A diver hooks a giant <part>clam</part> on the end of an <part>anchor</part> and shakes it hard over the deck. Rattle, rattle: out tumbles a pearl, then a crab, then a rusty spoon. Keep going, there's more in there. Give it a good <kanji>shake</kanji>.
振.on: The heavy clam swings back on its chain and bangs him right on the <sound>shin</sound>.
振.kun: He hops around the deck and flops onto a <sound>fu</sound>ton, rubbing his sore leg.

総.meaning: For the festival, the town strings one <part>thread</part> along the whole <part>public</part> high street, and every shop hangs a paper <part>heart</part> on it. From the hilltop it looks like one ribbon tying every door together. It's a <kanji>general</kanji> party: the whole town joins in.
総.on: When rain soaks the garland, the town washes the street with one giant bar of <sound>soa</sound>p that foams slowly for hours.
総.kun: Afterwards everyone shares one enormous plate of <sound>su</sound>shi, and every last piece of it gets eaten.

区.meaning: The city map is kept in a <part>drawer</part> at the town hall. One morning the mayor takes it out and, with a big pair of <part>scissors</part>, snips it into neat squares, one for each neighbourhood, each with its own mayor. Each piece is a <kanji>ward</kanji>.
区.on: Every ward gets its own <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock, and at noon they all chime at once across the city.
